ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=ax^{2}+2ax+1$ has only one common point A with the x-axis. The line passing through point A intersects the parabola at point B and the y-axis at point C, and point C is the midpoint of line segment AB. What is the analytical expression of the function corresponding to this parabola?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the parabola $y=ax^{2}+2ax+1$ has only one common point $A$ with the x-axis,\\
therefore, $\Delta=4a^{2}-4a=0$, solving this yields $a_{1}=0$ (discard), $a_{2}=1$,\\
therefore, the equation of the parabola is $\boxed{y=x^{2}+2x+1}$.
